note: The best-known difference. lè sè is the MOE reading and what everyone says; lā jī sounds mainland.

example.en: Remember to take out the trash.

note: MOE's Concised dictionary gives bāo guā (the Revised one bāo kuò). Teachers and news anchors say guā; casual speech is mostly bāo kuò.

note: Taiwan says shóu in every word (熟悉, 成熟, 很熟), and MOE's Concised dictionary lists shóu. The mainland standard is shú.

example.en: This mango isn't ripe yet.

note: Same 熟 = shóu rule, and 悉 keeps its 1st tone.

example.en: I'm not very familiar with this area.

note: Taiwan reads 血 as xiě in every word (流血, 血型, 血壓, 捐血). The mainland uses xuè in compounds.

note: MOE (like the mainland) says jué sè, but nearly everyone in Taiwan says jiǎo sè; same for 主角, 配角.

example.zh: 她在這部戲裡演一個很重要的角色。
example.en: She plays a very important role in this drama.

note: 暫 is zhàn in Taiwan (mainland zàn): 暫時, 暫停, 短暫.

example.en: I'm staying at a friend's place for now.

note: 期 is qí (2nd tone) in every word in Taiwan; the mainland reads it qī.

example.zh: 下個星期我要去高雄出差。
example.en: I'm going to Kaohsiung on a business trip next week.

note: Same 期 = qí rule.

example.zh: 這個學期我修了五門課。
example.en: I'm taking five courses this semester.

note: Same 期 = qí rule.

example.en: Please fill in today's date here.

note: Same 期 = qí rule.

note: 微 is wéi (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 微笑, 稍微, 微波爐, 輕微.

note: Same 微 = wéi rule.

example.en: I want to visit France next year.

note: Most Taiwanese say yǎ (3rd tone). MOE's main reading is yà, with yǎ listed as an accepted variant.

note: 究 is jiù (4th tone) in Taiwan's standard; yán jiū is also widely heard in casual speech.

example.en: He's researching Taiwanese history.

note: 髮 is fǎ (3rd tone) in Taiwan and keeps its tone; the mainland reads 发 (hair) as fà, neutral in 头发.

note: 質 is zhí (2nd tone) in Taiwan (except 人質 rén zhì). Taiwan says 品質 where the mainland says 质量.

example.en: The things at this shop are of good quality.

example.en: Lots of people like to vacation in Southeast Asia.

note: Same 究 = jiù rule. In Taiwan 研究所 is the everyday word for grad school.

example.en: I plan to take the grad school entrance exam next year.

note: Same 究 = jiù rule.

example.en: What exactly are you trying to say?

note: Same 髮 = fǎ rule.

example.en: You changed your hairstyle! It looks great.

note: Taiwan's word for shampoo (mainland 洗发水); 髮 is fǎ.

example.en: We're almost out of shampoo.

note: Same 質 = zhí rule.

example.zh: 這兩份工作的性質不太一樣。
example.en: The nature of these two jobs is rather different.

note: Same 質 = zhí rule. 很有氣質 is a common compliment.

example.en: She looks very elegant.

note: Same 質 = zhí rule.

example.en: He doesn't care much about material comforts.

note: Same 質 = zhí rule.

example.zh: 這所學校的學生素質很高。
example.en: The students at this school are of high caliber.

note: Same 質 = zhí rule. 有質感 (classy, well made) is very common in Taiwan.

example.en: This bag feels really well made.

note: Same 質 = zhí rule.

example.zh: 運動完要多補充蛋白質。
example.en: You should get more protein after working out.

note: Same 擁 = yǒng rule.

example.en: They hugged each other when they met.

note: Same 擁 = yǒng rule.

example.zh: 上下班時間捷運很擁擠。
example.en: The MRT is very crowded at rush hour.

note: 擊 is jí (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 攻擊, 打擊, 襲擊, 射擊.

example.zh: 這種狗不會主動攻擊人。
example.en: This kind of dog won't attack people unprovoked.

note: Same 擊 = jí rule.

example.zh: 這次失敗對他打擊很大。
example.en: This failure was a big blow to him.

note: Same 擊 = jí rule.

example.zh: 疫情對觀光業造成很大的衝擊。
example.en: The pandemic had a huge impact on tourism.

note: Same 績 = jī rule.

example.zh: 他這個月的業績是全公司第一。
example.en: His sales this month are the best in the whole company.

note: 蹟/跡 is jī in Taiwan (mainland 迹 jì): 古蹟, 奇蹟, 痕跡.

example.en: Tainan has many historic sites.

note: Same 蹟 = jī rule.

example.en: It's truly a miracle that he survived.

note: Same 跡 = jī rule.

example.zh: 桌上留下了杯子的痕跡。
example.en: The cup left a mark on the table.

note: 綜 is zòng (4th tone) in Taiwan: 綜合, 綜藝.

example.en: I'd like a mixed fruit juice.

note: Same 綜 = zòng rule.

example.en: My dad loves watching variety shows.

note: 寂 is jí (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 寂寞, 寂靜.

example.zh: 一個人住有時候會覺得寂寞。
example.en: Living alone, you sometimes feel lonely.

note: 夕 is xì (4th tone) in Taiwan: 夕陽, 除夕, 七夕.

example.en: The sunsets in Tamsui are famous.

note: Same 夕 = xì rule.

example.zh: 除夕全家人會一起圍爐。
example.en: On New Year's Eve the whole family gathers for the reunion dinner.

note: 息 is xí (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 利息, 訊息, 作息, 休息, 消息.

example.zh: 這家銀行的利息比較高。
example.en: This bank's interest is higher.

note: Same 息 = xí rule.

example.en: He keeps a very regular daily routine.

note: Same 惜 = xí rule.

example.en: Cherish the people around you.

note: Same 跌 = dié rule.

example.zh: 今天股市下跌了兩百點。
example.en: The stock market fell two hundred points today.

note: Same 突 = tú rule.

example.zh: 這項技術有了新的突破。
example.en: There's been a new breakthrough in this technology.

note: Same 突 = tú rule.

example.zh: 這兩個會議的時間衝突了。
example.en: These two meetings clash.

note: Same 檔 = dǎng rule.

example.en: Remember to save before you close it.

note: Same 檔 = dǎng rule.

example.zh: 他們去了一家很高檔的餐廳。
example.en: They went to a very upscale restaurant.

note: 傍 is bāng (1st tone) in 傍晚 in Taiwan.

example.zh: 傍晚的時候我常去河邊散步。
example.en: I often take a walk by the river at dusk.

note: Taiwan's word for topping up (mainland 充值); 儲 is chú.

example.en: My EasyCard needs topping up.

note: 椰 is yé (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 椰子, 椰奶.

example.en: I want to drink coconut water.

note: 偽 is wèi (4th tone) in Taiwan: 虛偽, 偽造, 偽裝.

example.en: I don't like fake people.

note: 播 is bò (4th tone) in Taiwan's standard; bō is also very common in speech.

example.zh: 你有聽到車站的廣播嗎？
example.en: Did you hear the station announcement?

note: Same 播 = bò rule (bō also heard).

example.en: The TV is showing the news.

note: MOE reading is bò; among younger people zhí bō is at least as common.

example.zh: 她每天晚上都會開直播。
example.en: She livestreams every evening.

note: Same 播 = bò rule (bō also heard).

example.zh: 她是很有名的新聞主播。
example.en: She's a very well-known news anchor.

note: 識 is shì (4th tone) in Taiwan: 常識, 意識, 共識, 認識, 知識.

example.en: That's just basic common sense.

note: Same 識 = shì rule.

example.zh: 他被送到醫院時已經失去意識。
example.en: He had already lost consciousness when he was taken to the hospital.

note: Same 識 = shì rule.

example.en: Everyone has yet to reach a consensus.

note: Most Taiwanese say yí (友誼, 聯誼). MOE's current main reading is yì, with yí listed as a variant.

example.zh: 我們的友誼已經超過二十年了。
example.en: Our friendship has lasted more than twenty years.

note: 蹈 is dào (4th tone) in Taiwan.

example.en: She has studied dance since she was little.

note: 諷 is fèng (4th tone) in Taiwan.

example.en: There's always sarcasm in the way he talks.

note: 菌 is jùn (4th tone) in Taiwan's standard: 細菌, 殺菌, 益生菌. jūn is also heard.

example.en: There are lots of germs on your phone.

note: Taiwan says yūn (1st tone) in 暈車, 暈船, 暈機; the mainland says yùn.

example.en: I get carsick easily on buses.

en: to get seasick; (slang) to fall hard for someone
note: Same yūn rule. In Taiwan slang 暈船 also means getting hopelessly infatuated.

example.zh: 去綠島的路上很多人暈船。
example.en: Lots of people got seasick on the way to Green Island.

note: Taiwan says dāng tiān; the mainland standard is dàng tiān for 'the same day'.

example.en: We'll go and come back the same day, without staying overnight.

note: 夾 is jiá (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 夾子, 夾克, 皮夾, 夾娃娃.

example.en: Please use the tongs to pick up the bread.

note: Taiwan's everyday word for wallet (mainland 钱包); 夾 is jiá.

example.en: I left my wallet at home.

note: 寧 is níng (2nd tone) in Taiwan even in 寧願 and 寧可; the mainland says nìng.

example.zh: 我寧願走路也不想等公車。
example.en: I'd rather walk than wait for the bus.

note: Taiwan keeps both syllables 3rd tone (sandhi: qiáo qiǎo); the mainland says qiāo qiāo. 悄悄話 = whispered secrets.

example.en: He quietly slipped out of the classroom.

note: Taiwan's word for cabbage (mainland 卷心菜 / 包菜). Everyone says gāo lì cài, though MOE's dictionary reading is gāo lí cài.

example.en: I'd like an order of stir-fried cabbage.

note: Everyone in Taiwan says zhà for deep-frying (炸雞, 油炸, 炸物), although dictionaries on both sides give zhá.

example.zh: 我們晚上叫炸雞外送好不好？
example.en: Shall we order fried chicken delivery tonight?

note: Taiwan says tà shí; the mainland says tā shi (1st tone + neutral).

example.zh: 把工作做完心裡比較踏實。
example.en: I feel more at ease once the work is done.

note: MOE reads 骨頭 as gú tou (2nd-tone 骨, only in this word); the mainland standard is now gǔ tou. Taiwan speech often gives 頭 a full tóu.

example.en: This pot of soup is simmered from bones.

note: Most Taiwanese say mò for 膜 (面膜, 保鮮膜), which MOE's Revised dictionary lists first; the newer Concised dictionary gives mó, like the mainland.

example.en: I put on a face mask before bed.

note: MOE dictionaries give zhāo jí, so you'll see it in zhuyin, but most people say zháo jí like the mainland.

example.en: Don't get anxious; tell me slowly.

note: Everyday Taiwan speech keeps the full tone on 得 (dé); MOE dictionaries still list the neutral tone, like the mainland.

example.zh: 這家餐廳值得再來一次。
example.en: This restaurant is worth coming back to.

en: can't bear to part with; reluctant
note: Taiwan says shě bù dé with full tones. MOE keeps 不 full but still lists a neutral 得; the mainland reads both light.

example.en: I can't bear to leave Taiwan.

note: The middle 不 keeps its 4th tone in Taiwan speech; the mainland reads it neutral.

example.en: If we don't leave now we won't make it.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 氣 (qì), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: I'm so tired I have no strength to talk.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 氣 (qì), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 他的脾氣很好，很少生氣。
example.en: He's good-tempered and rarely gets angry.

note: Everyday Taiwan speech keeps the full tone on 氣 (qì); MOE dictionaries still list the neutral tone, like the mainland.

example.zh: 今天運氣真好，一出門就等到公車。
example.en: What luck today: the bus came the moment I stepped out.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 氣 (qì), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: He's stingy and never treats anyone.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 量 (liáng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 這件事我要先跟家人商量。
example.en: I need to talk this over with my family first.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 拾 (shí), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 出門前先把房間收拾一下。
example.en: Tidy up your room before going out.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 意 (yì), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: That's a good idea!

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 理 (lǐ), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: What you say makes a lot of sense.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 矩 (jǔ), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 每個家庭都有自己的規矩。
example.en: Every family has its own rules.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 萄 (táo), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: This bunch of grapes is so sweet.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 璃 (lí), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Careful, there's broken glass on the floor.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 水 (shuǐ), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: This job pays pretty well.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 夫 (fū), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Her husband is an engineer.

note: Taiwan speech usually gives 子 its full 3rd tone here; MOE dictionaries list qī zi for 'wife', like the mainland.

example.en: He and his wife have been married for ten years.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 戚 (qī), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: At Lunar New Year we visit relatives to pay our respects.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 話 (huà), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: He's great at telling jokes.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 分 (fèn), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Please show your ID card.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 分 (fèn), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 能認識你也是一種緣分。
example.en: Getting to know you is a kind of fate too.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 屈 (qū), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: She felt wronged and started crying.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 處 (chù), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 早睡早起對身體有好處。
example.en: Going to bed and getting up early is good for your health.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 巴 (bā), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Please open your mouth.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 巴 (bā), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: The puppy keeps wagging its tail.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 巴 (bā), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 他的下巴長了一顆痘痘。
example.en: He's got a pimple on his chin.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 股 (gǔ), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Your butt hurts if you sit too long.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 袋 (dài), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: My mind went completely blank.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 袋 (dài), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: The keys are in my pocket.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 甲 (jiǎ), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Your nails need cutting.

note: Taiwan speech usually gives the 頭 suffix a full tóu (石頭, 枕頭, 饅頭); MOE dictionaries list neutral tou, like the mainland.

example.zh: 河邊有很多漂亮的石頭。
example.en: There are lots of pretty stones by the river.

note: Everyday Taiwan speech keeps the full tone on 頭 (tóu); MOE dictionaries still list the neutral tone, like the mainland.

example.zh: 這個枕頭太高了，睡起來脖子會痛。
example.en: This pillow is too high; my neck hurts when I sleep on it.

note: Everyday Taiwan speech keeps the full tone on 星 (xīng); MOE dictionaries still list the neutral tone, like the mainland.

example.zh: 山上可以看到很多星星。
example.en: You can see lots of stars up in the mountains.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 屜 (tì), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: The scissors are in the second drawer.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 瑰 (guī), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: He gave me a bouquet of roses.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 心 (xīn), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 下午我們準備了一些點心。
example.en: We've prepared some snacks for the afternoon.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 塗 (tú), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 我真糊塗，又忘了帶手機。
example.en: How scatterbrained of me; I forgot my phone again.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 糊 (hú), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 這張照片拍得有點模糊。
example.en: This photo came out a bit blurry.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 實 (shí), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 老實說，我不太喜歡這個顏色。
example.en: Honestly, I don't much like this color.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 方 (fāng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: He's very generous with his friends.

en: to dress up; style of dress
note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 扮 (bàn), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: She's dressed up beautifully today.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 呼 (hū), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 他看到我，就跟我打招呼。
example.en: He greeted me when he saw me.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 乎 (hū), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 我不在乎別人怎麼看我。
example.en: I don't care how others see me.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 付 (fù), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 工作太多，我快應付不來了。
example.en: There's too much work; I can barely cope.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 服 (fú), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: I really admire his courage.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 誤 (wù), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 不好意思，耽誤你的時間了。
example.en: Sorry for taking up your time.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 士 (shì), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: The nurse took my temperature.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 傅 (fù), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 這位師傅做麵包做了三十年。
example.en: This master baker has been making bread for thirty years.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 量 (liàng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: Unity is strength.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 務 (wù), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: This mission is no simple matter.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 牌 (pái), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 牛肉麵是這家店的招牌。
example.en: Beef noodle soup is this shop's signature dish.

note: 究 is jiù (4th tone) in Taiwan and keeps its tone; the mainland says jiǎng jiu.

example.en: He's very particular about coffee.

note: No 兒 in Taiwan.

example.en: I was almost late this morning.

note: No 兒 in Taiwan.

example.en: There's a painting hanging on the wall.

note: The dictionary reading is biàn; many Taiwanese say piàn (also in 一遍). Recognize it, but biàn is the safe choice.

example.en: This kind of situation is very common.

note: 括 is guā in MOE's standard, and guā hào (also 括弧 guā hú) is common in Taiwan classrooms; kuò hào is heard too.

example.en: Please write the answer inside the parentheses.

note: Both MOE dictionaries give yái, but in real life you will mostly hear xuán yá.

example.en: Don't get too close to the edge of the cliff.

note: 淆 is yáo in Taiwan (mainland xiáo).

example.en: These two characters are easily confused.

note: MOE reading is sāo; sōu is also heard in casual speech.

example.en: Several fishing boats are docked in the harbor.

note: 酵 is xiào in Taiwan (mainland jiào): 酵素, 發酵, 酵母.

example.zh: 這種水果含有很多酵素。
example.en: This fruit contains a lot of enzymes.

note: Same 酵 = xiào rule.

example.en: The dough needs to ferment for an hour.

note: 酪 is luò in Taiwan (mainland lào): 乳酪, 酪梨, 優酪乳.

example.en: I'd like to buy a piece of cheesecake.

note: Taiwan's word for avocado (mainland 牛油果); 酪 is luò.

example.zh: 這家的酪梨牛奶很好喝。
example.en: This shop's avocado milk is really good.

note: Taiwan reads 剝 as bō everywhere; the mainland uses bāo for the everyday verb.

example.zh: 你可以幫我把橘子剝皮嗎？
example.en: Can you peel the orange for me?

note: 殼 is always ké in Taiwan; the mainland uses qiào in 地壳, 甲壳.

example.zh: 地震是地殼變動造成的。
example.en: Earthquakes are caused by movements of the earth's crust.

note: Read sào here, not zào (the mainland writes this topping 肉臊 / 臊子). 肉燥飯 is a classic Taiwanese dish.

example.en: I'd like a bowl of minced pork rice.

note: 檜 is kuài in Taiwan (mainland guì). Alishan is famous for its 檜木.

example.zh: 阿里山有很多千年檜木。
example.en: Alishan has many thousand-year-old cypress trees.

en: to put on the wanted list
note: 緝 is qì in Taiwan (mainland jī): 通緝, 緝毒.

example.zh: 警方已經通緝那名嫌犯。
example.en: Police have put that suspect on the wanted list.

note: MOE's Concised dictionary reads 天秤 as tiān píng, but most people say tiān chèng zuò, like the mainland. Both are understood.

example.en: I'm a Libra.

note: 紮 is zhá in Taiwan (mainland 包扎 bāo zā).

example.zh: 護理師幫我把傷口包紮好了。
example.en: The nurse bandaged my wound.

note: 堤 is tí in Taiwan (mainland dī): 堤防, 河堤. 提防 (to guard against) is also tí fáng, mainland dī fang.

example.zh: 我們沿著堤防騎腳踏車。
example.en: We rode our bikes along the levee.

note: MOE's Concised dictionary reads 勁 as jìng (起勁, 使勁, 幹勁); the mainland says jìn.

example.en: They're chatting away with great gusto.

en: to hold hostage; to seize by force
note: 挾 is xiá in MOE's Concised dictionary and in Taiwan news speech; the mainland (and MOE's Revised dictionary) say xié.

example.en: The criminal took a hostage.

note: Taiwan says wǎn xióng (MOE's Concised reading; the older Revised dictionary has huǎn). The mainland says huàn xióng.

example.zh: 動物園新來了一隻浣熊。
example.en: A raccoon has just arrived at the zoo.

note: MOE dictionaries give lè gǔ, but in daily life people say lèi gǔ (and 肋排 lèi pái), same as the mainland.

example.zh: 他騎車摔倒，斷了兩根肋骨。
example.en: He fell off his scooter and broke two ribs.

note: 柏 is bó in Taiwan's standard (柏油, 松柏); the mainland says bǎi except in names like 柏林.

example.zh: 這條柏油路是去年才鋪的。
example.en: This asphalt road was only laid last year.

note: Same 微 = wéi rule. Taiwanese mostly use LINE, so this comes up when talking about China.

example.zh: 他在上海工作，所以都用微信聯絡。
example.en: He works in Shanghai, so he keeps in touch through WeChat.

note: Same 髮 = fǎ rule. Everyday Taiwan speech prefers 剪頭髮.

example.zh: 巷口那家理髮店很便宜。
example.en: The barbershop at the end of the alley is cheap.

note: In Taiwan 質量 mostly means 'mass' in physics; for 'quality' say 品質.

example.zh: 物理課今天教質量和重量的差別。
example.en: Today's physics class covered the difference between mass and weight.

note: Same 擊 = jí rule.

example.en: The village was attacked last night.

note: Same 擊 = jí rule.

example.zh: 他當兵的時候射擊成績很好。
example.en: He scored well in shooting during his military service.

note: Same 夕 = xì rule.

example.zh: 七夕那天餐廳都客滿了。
example.en: The restaurants were all fully booked on Qixi.

en: to turn off the engine; to stall
note: 熄 is xí in Taiwan (mainland xī): 熄火, 熄燈, 熄滅.

example.zh: 停紅燈的時候機車突然熄火了。
example.en: The scooter suddenly stalled at the red light.

note: 框 is kuāng (1st tone) in Taiwan (mainland kuàng): 相框, 框架, 框框; likewise 眶 in 眼眶.

example.zh: 我買了一個相框放全家福。
example.en: I bought a frame for the family photo.

note: 儲 is chú (2nd tone) in Taiwan's standard: 儲蓄, 儲存, 儲值. chǔ is also heard.

example.zh: 他每個月都會儲蓄一萬塊。
example.en: He saves ten thousand NT every month.

note: 樸 is pú (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 樸素, 樸實.

example.en: She usually dresses very plainly.

note: 帆 is fán (2nd tone) in Taiwan: 帆船, 帆布.

example.en: There are a few sailboats out on the sea.

note: 鞠 is jú (2nd tone) in Taiwan.

example.en: He bowed deeply to his teacher.

note: Taiwan reads 載 as zài for both 'carry' and 'record'; the mainland uses zǎi in 记载, 刊载, 连载.

example.zh: 這件事在史書上有記載。
example.en: This event is recorded in the history books.

note: Same 載 = zài rule.

example.zh: 這篇文章刊載在昨天的報紙上。
example.en: This article was published in yesterday's paper.

note: 剖 is pǒu (3rd tone) in Taiwan: 解剖, 剖腹產, 剖析.

example.en: We have to dissect a frog in biology class.

note: 穴 is xuè (4th tone) in Taiwan's standard: 洞穴, 穴道, 巢穴. The mainland says xué.

example.en: Bats live in caves.

note: Same 誼 = yí habit (MOE's main reading is yì). In Taiwan 聯誼 usually means a group date or mixer.

example.zh: 我們系下禮拜要跟護理系聯誼。
example.en: Our department is having a mixer with the nursing department next week.

note: 噸 is dùn (4th tone) in Taiwan (mainland dūn).

example.zh: 這輛卡車可以載十公噸的貨。
example.en: This truck can carry ten metric tons of cargo.

note: 拙 is zhuó (2nd tone) in Taiwan.

example.en: His movements are a bit clumsy.

note: 淑 is shú (2nd tone) in Taiwan, like 叔.

example.en: She's dressed very ladylike today.

note: 辱 is rù (4th tone) in Taiwan: 侮辱, 羞辱, 恥辱.

example.en: Saying that is an insult to me.

note: 署 is shù (4th tone) in Taiwan when it means to sign or arrange: 簽署, 部署, 署名. In agency names (警政署) it is shǔ.

example.zh: 兩國昨天簽署了合作協議。
example.en: The two countries signed a cooperation agreement yesterday.

note: 褐 is hé (2nd tone) in Taiwan. Everyday speech prefers 咖啡色.

example.zh: 他穿著一件褐色的外套。
example.en: He's wearing a brown jacket.

note: Taiwan says méng gǔ, as in 蒙古烤肉 (Mongolian barbecue); the mainland says měng gǔ.

example.zh: 我一直很想去蒙古看草原。
example.en: I've always wanted to go see the grasslands in Mongolia.

en: to cheat on one's partner; to do the splits
note: Taiwan says pī tuǐ. The 'two-timing' sense started as Taiwan slang.

example.zh: 她發現男朋友劈腿，就分手了。
example.en: She found out her boyfriend was cheating and broke up with him.

en: grand finale; the last big act
note: 軸 is always zhóu in Taiwan; the mainland says yā zhòu.

example.zh: 今晚的壓軸表演是五月天。
example.en: Tonight's finale act is Mayday.

note: Taiwan says lóng zhào; the mainland says lǒng zhào.

example.en: The whole mountain is shrouded in thick fog.

note: 削 is xuè (4th tone) in Taiwan in 剝削, 削減, 削弱; the mainland says xuē. (For peeling, both sides say xiāo.)

example.zh: 他覺得老闆在剝削員工。
example.en: He feels the boss is exploiting the employees.

en: to cut; to reduce (a budget etc.)
note: Same 削 = xuè rule.

example.zh: 公司決定削減明年的預算。
example.en: The company decided to cut next year's budget.

note: MOE's main reading is pǐ (pì is listed as a variant), but jié pì is what you usually hear in Taiwan.

example.zh: 他有潔癖，每天都要拖地。
example.en: He's a clean freak and has to mop the floor every day.

note: MOE's main reading is biān fú, same as the mainland; biǎn is a listed variant that many Taiwanese use (蝙蝠俠).

example.zh: 晚上公園裡有蝙蝠在飛。
example.en: Bats fly around the park at night.

note: 淋 is always lín in Taiwan; the mainland reads lìn only in this word (淋雨, 淋浴 are lín on both sides).

example.zh: 淋病可以用抗生素治療。
example.en: Gonorrhea can be treated with antibiotics.

note: 縛 is fú (2nd tone) in Taiwan (mainland fù).

example.zh: 他不想被傳統觀念束縛。
example.en: He doesn't want to be bound by traditional ideas.

note: Taiwan says huá jī with a full 1st tone (mainland huá ji). MOE also lists a classical reading gǔ jī that nobody uses.

example.en: The way he walks is comical.

note: 薄 is bò in this word on both sides; Taiwan keeps the full 2nd tone on 荷.

example.zh: 我喜歡薄荷口味的口香糖。
example.en: I like mint-flavored gum.

note: Everyday Taiwan speech keeps the full tone on 頭 (tóu); MOE dictionaries still list the neutral tone, like the mainland.

example.zh: 我早餐買了一個饅頭夾蛋。
example.en: I bought a steamed bun with egg for breakfast.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 餅 (bǐng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: I'd like a sesame flatbread with a fried dough stick.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 餅 (bǐng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 中秋節大家都會送月餅。
example.en: Everyone gives mooncakes at Mid-Autumn Festival.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 狸 (lí), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 這個故事的主角是一隻狐狸。
example.en: The main character of this story is a fox.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 箏 (zhēng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: The kids are flying kites in the park.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 籠 (lóng), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.zh: 元宵節小朋友會提燈籠。
example.en: Children carry lanterns at the Lantern Festival.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 伙 (huǒ), as MOE lists it; the mainland reads it in neutral tone.

example.en: This guy is late again.
